extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) dealing with chemical and alloy inventions in Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Examination guideline for patentability, description/claim requirements, novelty and inventive-step assessment of chemical (polymorphs, enantiomers, catalysts, selection inventions) and alloy inventions. Used to decide whether claims meet statutory requirements and how to evaluate supporting disclosure and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polymorphic form inventive-step criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention relating to polymorphic form ... is considered having inventive step if it has clearly different qualitative effect compared to the compound disclosed in the prior art, or if it has clearly different quantitative effect compared to that in the prior art regardless of qualitative effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description must state the effect clearly even if there is no test data comparing with the prior art; if the effect is doubtful it shall be proved concretely by submitting evidence such as comparative test data trusted by applicant/patentee after filing date. (See Supreme Court verdict references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inorganic compound with specific feature — claim and inventive-step review
rubrics_metrics.description: For an inorganic compound, name and chemical formula alone may not specify the subject matter because physical property or configuration (microstructure, e.g., crystal form, unit surface area) can differ; therefore, review of specific property shall be included in the claim regardless of explicit statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether it can be expected that the compound with specific property stated in the specification is produced by adoption/combination of components given the level of technology; do not determine inventive step without taking account of specific property differences even when name/formula are the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-use (compound 'for ~') construction
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of a chemical compound, use limitation stated by 'for~' (e.g. 'Chemical compound Z for Y') is considered as indicating only utility, and is construed as the chemical compound without the use limitation (e.g. 'Chemical compound Z').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claimed chemical compound is disclosed in the prior art, the chemical compound with a use limitation is deemed to lack novelty. Example: 'Chemical compound Z for killing insects' reads as 'Chemical compound Z' and lacks novelty if Z is in prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection invention inventive-step requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For a selection invention to be recognized as involving inventive step over a generic prior-art disclosure, all species included in the selection should have different effect from that of the prior art invention qualitatively or quantitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific compounds are merely selected from a wide range without stated favorable effect, or can be easily selected by a skilled person because properties are expectable, inventive step is lacking. Unexpected favorable property of selected species supports inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enantiomer novelty (disclosure from racemate)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an enantiomer is specifically disclosed in the prior art while a racemate (racemic mixture) is stated, the enantiomer is considered to lack novelty. If the existence of the enantiomer can be found out from the disclosure or easily carried out by a skilled person, it may be deemed disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court verdict examples: where prior art disclosed racemate and teaching allowed identification/preparation of individual enantiomers, the enantiomer claim was anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enantiomer inventive-step (property-based) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If an enantiomer is not disclosed in detail in the prior art, inventive step shall be determined by considering whether it has extraordinary effect in its chemical/physical properties compared to the disclosed racemate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For use inventions of enantiomers, assess whether the enantiomer has different effect compared to use of the racemate. Extraordinary or different effects support inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-invention of enantiomers — two-prong requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A use invention of a specific enantiomer can be patented only if (1) prior art stating use of racemate does not disclose the enantiomer's use in detail, and (2) the enantiomer has different effect from the racemate disclosed qualitatively or quantitatively based on specific physical/chemical properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference need not cover all effects — it suffices that some effects differ. Difference cannot be denied merely because a skilled person might find it by simple repeated tests. Prior knowledge that an enantiomer may be better does not automatically mean the specific enantiomer's use is obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst novelty — reaction context requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is impossible to determine patentability of a catalyst without considering the reaction in which the catalyst is used; novelty is determined based on the composition of the catalyst and the type of reaction in which the catalyst is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A catalyst disclosed outside the context of the same reaction may not anticipate; consider both composition and reaction type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst inventive-step — different-reaction case
rubrics_metrics.description: If a disclosed catalyst has composition identical or similar to the claimed catalyst but is used in a different reaction or reaction type, and the claimed catalyst's effect (versus no catalyst) is recognized, the invention may have inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether change of reaction context yields a recognized beneficial effect; compare to case without a catalyst.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst inventive-step — novel composition case
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no disclosed catalyst of same or similar composition for the reaction in which the claimed catalyst is intended to be used, the claimed catalyst is deemed to have inventive step by comparing its effect with a case without the catalyst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate effect of catalyst versus no-catalyst baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst inventive-step — supported vs unsupported selection
rubrics_metrics.description: For selection between supported and unsupported catalyst systems, consider the technical meaning stated in the specification or whether an extraordinary effect is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporter may serve functions (produce active catalyst, reduce cost, improve mechanical property). Unless the specification states technical meaning or effect, form (supported/unsupported) alone does not imply specific differences. See Patent Court verdicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alloy inventions — when alloy guidelines apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter applies to an invention relating to alloying technique (C22C). For other fields, apply if alloy structure/property/use are specified through alloying components and numerical limitation of each component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims merely recite that a product comprises an alloy plating formed by a plating solution (without alloy structure/property/composition ranges), alloy guidelines may not apply. But a manufacturing method claim that includes specific alloy component ranges does trigger the alloy guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description requirements — grounds and embodiment for numeric composition limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If a numerical limitation to a composition range is stated in claims, grounds and embodiment should be described in the description; exception when it is recognized that the alloy can be specified and carried out easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum and minimum limits must be clear; ambiguous terms not allowed. For every limited range state reasons for limits, significant effect across the whole span, and concrete reasons for synergy of elements. Failure to disclose may lead to cyclic tests/trial-and-error and not satisfy disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description requirements — necessity of test data for alloys
rubrics_metrics.description: Because alloy effects are difficult to predict, it is necessary to disclose results of tests (embodiment, example of test, comparative example) to prove the alloy's effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If test data are described, specify target, method, test requirements, and technical effect not achieved by prior art so that a skilled person can carry out the invention. Court verdicts show lack of comparative testing can defeat asserted effects across claimed range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiment sufficiency criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an embodiment is specified is determined: (1) at least one embodiment with a composition range consistent with the claims satisfies Article 42(3)i; (2) if an embodiment lacks essential alloying elements or includes non-claimed alloying elements (except inevitable impurities), it's not representative; (3) specific content of each alloying element should be specified in embodiment; (4) effects should be specifically stated (not abstract/subjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One representative embodiment may be enough for disclosure, but proving significant effect across a numerical range often requires more than a single example (esp. near range limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing method disclosure for alloys
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the claimed invention is directed to a product alloy, the manufacturing method (melting, casting, heating, machining, etc.) should be stated in detail for a skilled person to reproduce the alloy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A manufacturing method can be simply stated if the alloy can be manufactured by normal methods. Distinguish between smelting/refining methods and methods that alter structure/property of a parent metal (these can be distinct inventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim requirements — limitation of alloy composition
rubrics_metrics.description: An alloy's composition that achieves intended properties or use should be specified; reciting only alloying elements without composition ranges typically fails to particularly point out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify composition ranges for each alloying element (e.g., C:a-b wt%, Si:c-d wt%, ...). When issuing a rejection for lack of particulation, state reasonable grounds in detail after reviewing full disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim requirements — overly broad composition ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: If a composition range is too broad (e.g., constituents with 0-100% ranges), except special cases, the claim should be deemed not clearly described because the alloy's structure/property/use can change across the range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases include homogeneous solid solution, amorphous alloy, commercial alloy notifying its composition, and alloys included in industrial standards (KS, ASTM, JIS, DIN), where composition ranges may not need specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impurity recitation and allowable ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: An element in claims cannot be treated as an impurity unless defined as such in the specification or by common knowledge; allowable ranges of impurities should be stated in the description and upper limits specified in claims when impurities greatly impact property/use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable impurity ranges are typically given as an upper limit (e.g., '0.3 wt% or less'). When possible, state ranges in the description for publication clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of new matter — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments such as deletion of an element, addition of a new element, change of a composition range, addition/expansion of new property or use, etc., are recognized as addition of new matter relative to the original specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For alloy inventions (numerical-limitation inventions), adding alloying elements or composition ranges not in the original specification is generally new matter. However, reduction of a composition range without change of property/use may not be new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment adding numerical range — new matter test
rubrics_metrics.description: When claim is amended to include a new numerical range, if the new numerical range and the reasons for it are not disclosed in the original description, it is deemed an addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: adding specific wt% ranges in amended claims when not present originally constitutes new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments that do not constitute new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the numerical range is obvious or inherent from the disclosure of the specification and ordinary skill, the amendment can be considered correction of error rather than addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reducing upper limit of a range to one already described as appropriate in the description (e.g., 200-10000 μm → 200-6000 μm when 200-6000 μm described as appropriate). Use embodiments/comparative examples to justify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty — identity criteria for alloy inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of an alloy invention is determined by whether each element of an alloy is identical, its composition range and structure are identical, and whether its utility (property or use) is identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For manufacturing methods, consider identity of the alloy and identity of the manufacturing process. If composition and structure are identical, perceived property differences do not make the subject matter distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty — method to determine identity and selection exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing claimed alloy with prior art: if composition and structure are identical, effects cannot be different and inventions deemed substantially identical; partial overlap of composition ranges can still be identical unless selection of a specific range has critical meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish patentability based on a selected composition range from prior art, the selection must have critical meaning (e.g., provide unexpected effect). Court case references illustrate application.
